cohort: The study included 80 women with pregnancy-induced hypertension and perinatal infection after cesarean section (study group) and 80 pregnant women with hypertension without perinatal infection during cesarean section (control group).
finding: Maternal levels of inflammatory factors and FEIR were significantly higher, while FEER and RBC-ICR were lower in the group with perinatal infection, demonstrating good predictive value for perinatal infection in women with pregnancy-induced hypertension after cesarean section.
mod_finding: The observed changes in inflammatory factors and RBC immune indices are relevant for women with pregnancy-induced hypertension who underwent cesarean section.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken prior to or during perinatal infection in women who had undergone cesarean section for pregnancy-induced hypertension.
